senses.definition: Words on or near something that tell what it is or give useful information about it.
senses.example: The label on the bottle says what is inside.

senses.definition: To put a name or words that explain something on or near it.
senses.example: Please label each cup with a name.

senses.definition: Work that takes time and effort, often physical work.
senses.example: Building the stone wall took a lot of labor.

senses.definition: To work very hard or make an effort to do something.
senses.example: They labored all morning to clear the branches off the trail.

senses.definition: A cord used to hold parts of a shoe or clothing together.
senses.example: One lace on my sneaker came loose.

senses.definition: Thin cloth with an open pattern of holes and threads.
senses.example: The edge of the costume was trimmed with lace.

senses.definition: To put a cord through holes and tighten it, often on a shoe.
senses.example: We laced our skates before walking to the rink.

senses.definition: To be without something you need or want.
senses.example: The recipe lacked enough salt to bring out the flavor.

senses.definition: The state of not having enough of something.
senses.example: The team practiced indoors for lack of a dry field.

senses.definition: A tool with two long sides joined by steps for climbing.
senses.example: We carried the ladder to the bookshelf so Dad could reach the top shelf.

senses.definition: A large spoon with a deep bowl and often a long handle, used to serve liquids.
senses.example: The cook filled each bowl with a ladle of stew.

senses.definition: To scoop or pour a liquid using a deep spoon.
senses.example: I helped ladle soup into the bowls.

senses.definition: To fall behind or take longer than something else.
senses.example: Our wagon lagged behind as we climbed the hill.

senses.definition: A delay between something happening and its result showing up.
senses.example: There was a short lag between pushing the button and seeing the light.

senses.definition: A shallow body of water separated from a larger body of water by a strip of land or a reef.
senses.example: The narrow sandbar protected the lagoon from the ocean waves.

senses.definition: A large area of water surrounded by land.
senses.example: A family of ducks swam across the lake.

senses.definition: A time when water near the top of a lake mixes with water from farther down.
senses.example: Cold autumn weather and wind helped bring on lake turnover.

senses.definition: A young sheep.
senses.example: The lamb followed its mother across the field.

senses.definition: A device that gives light.
senses.example: I turned on the lamp beside my bed.

senses.definition: The solid part of Earth’s surface that is not covered by water.
senses.example: After three hours at sea we could finally see land.

senses.definition: To come down to a surface or bring an aircraft down to a surface.
senses.example: The bird landed on the top rail of the fence.

senses.definition: To get something you worked for or hoped for.
senses.example: Maya practiced her lines and landed the part in the play.

senses.definition: The parts of an aircraft that support it while it is on the ground or another landing surface.
senses.example: The plane lowered its landing gear before its wheels touched the runway.

senses.definition: Surrounded by land with no coast on the open ocean.
senses.example: Switzerland is landlocked, so a ship from the ocean has to use a river to reach it.

senses.definition: A noticeable feature or building that helps you know where you are.
senses.example: The water tower was our landmark when we looked for the trail.

senses.definition: An important event or step in the history of something.
senses.example: The first library in town was a landmark in the effort to make books available to everyone.

senses.definition: All the natural and built features you can see across an area of land.
senses.example: Fields and low hills filled the landscape.

senses.definition: A picture of a wide view of land.
senses.example: Nia painted a landscape of the coast.

senses.definition: To change how an outdoor area looks or works, often by arranging plants, paths, or soil.
senses.example: The neighbors landscaped the yard with a path and several small trees.

senses.definition: A narrow road or a marked strip for one row of traffic or one person in a race.
senses.example: The bus moved into the right lane before turning.

senses.definition: A way people use words or signs to share meaning with each other.
senses.example: Our school librarian reads stories in more than one language.

senses.definition: The flat area across the top of your legs when you sit.
senses.example: I set the book in my lap before opening it.

senses.definition: One complete trip around a track or course.
senses.example: We rode one lap around the park.

senses.definition: To touch something gently again and again, as small waves do.
senses.example: Water lapped against the side of the boat.

senses.definition: Bigger than many others in size, number, or amount.
senses.example: We chose a large box for all the books.

senses.definition: Coming after all the others in a list or group.
senses.example: I was the last runner to cross the finish line.

senses.definition: Happening most recently before now.
senses.example: Last Friday we went to the aquarium.

senses.definition: To continue for an amount of time or stay usable.
senses.example: The concert lasted about an hour.

senses.definition: Happening after the expected or usual time.
senses.example: The bus was late because of the snow.

senses.definition: Near the end of a certain time.
senses.example: We picked the last tomatoes in late October.

senses.definition: After the time when you were expected to come or finish.
senses.example: My brother woke up late on Saturday.

senses.definition: After the time you are talking about, or in the future.
senses.example: We can finish the puzzle later.

senses.definition: Coming after another time, date, or event.
senses.example: We caught a later bus because we missed the first one.

senses.definition: A measure in degrees of how far north or south a place is from the equator.
senses.example: A place at 30 degrees north latitude is north of the equator.

senses.definition: Freedom to make some choices about how to do something.
senses.example: Our teacher gave us latitude to choose how we would share our research.

senses.definition: To make sounds with your voice when something is funny or you feel happy.
senses.example: The puppet made the whole class laugh.

senses.definition: The sound made by someone who finds something funny.
senses.example: I recognized his laugh from the other room.

senses.definition: To send something into the air, onto water, or into space to begin using it.
senses.example: We launched the paper plane from the top step.

senses.definition: To start a new activity or introduce something people can use.
senses.example: Our class launched a campaign to collect winter coats.

senses.definition: The first time something is sent, started, or offered.
senses.example: The launch of the boat drew a crowd to the shore.

senses.definition: Clothes and other cloth items that need washing, are being washed, or have just been washed.
senses.example: We folded the clean laundry after dinner.

senses.definition: Melted rock that reaches Earth’s surface, or the rock it makes after cooling.
senses.example: Lava flowed out of the opening and cooled into dark rock.

senses.definition: An area of short grass people care for near a building or in a public place.
senses.example: We spread a blanket on the lawn for lunch.

senses.definition: To put something down, often so it rests in a flat position. The past form is “laid.”
senses.example: Rosa laid a clean cloth over the table.

senses.definition: To produce and leave an egg.
senses.example: One hen laid a brown egg this morning.

senses.definition: Rested or stretched out flat. For this meaning, “lay” is a past form of “lie.”
senses.example: The cat lay in the sunshine.

senses.definition: One sheet, coating, or level that rests on top of or under another.
senses.example: We spread a layer of jam between the two pieces of cake.

senses.definition: To put sheets or levels of things on top of one another.
senses.example: Mina layered cardboard and cloth to make a strong cover.

senses.definition: Unwilling to work or use much effort, or slow and relaxed.
senses.example: It was a lazy afternoon and we read on the porch.

senses.definition: To guide people or animals by showing them where to go or what to do.
senses.example: We took turns leading the group down the trail.

senses.definition: A position ahead of the other people or teams in a contest.
senses.example: The blue team kept its lead until the final minute.

senses.definition: A heavy, soft metal that was once used for many things, including weights and old pipes.
senses.example: The museum label said the old weight was made of lead.

senses.definition: A usually flat part of a plant that often uses light to make food for the plant. The plural is “leaves.”
senses.example: I found a maple leaf with orange edges.

senses.definition: To turn through the pages of something quickly.
senses.example: I leafed through the magazine to find the train map.

senses.definition: Dead leaves and other small pieces of plants that collect on top of the soil.
senses.example: The leaf litter under the trees slowly broke into little pieces.

senses.definition: A small passage in a leaf that carries water or sugars through it.
senses.example: Tiny veins spread outward from the middle of the leaf.

senses.definition: To jump, often far or high.
senses.example: A little frog leaped from a rock into the pond.

senses.definition: A jump or a large, sudden change.
senses.example: The team made a leap from last place to second.

senses.definition: To get knowledge or a skill by study, practice, or experience.
senses.example: I learned to tie my shoes by watching my brother.

senses.definition: To find out some information.
senses.example: We learned that the path was closed for repairs.

senses.definition: Lowest in amount or degree.
senses.example: The corner seat gets the least sunlight in the morning.

senses.definition: Less than anything or anyone else in the group.
senses.example: That is the game I like least.

senses.definition: The smallest positive number that is a multiple of each of two or more given positive whole numbers.
senses.example: The least common multiple of three and four is 12.

senses.definition: A strong, flexible material made by treating animal skin.
senses.example: My leather work gloves are soft enough to bend.

senses.definition: To go away from a place or person.
senses.example: We left the park before the gates closed.

senses.definition: To let something stay in one place or condition when you go away or stop working on it.
senses.example: Please leave the note on the table.

senses.definition: To not include a person, item, or detail.
senses.example: If you leave out the date, we won’t know which page came first.

senses.definition: A talk that teaches or explains something to a group.
senses.example: The wildlife expert gave a lecture about owls.

senses.definition: To give a teaching talk, or to speak at length about how someone should behave.
senses.example: Grandpa lectured us about putting our tools away.

senses.definition: A small electronic part that gives off light when electricity flows through it in the proper direction.
senses.example: A green LED lights up when the speaker is charged.

senses.definition: On the side opposite your right side.
senses.example: Raise your left hand if you would like to read first.

senses.definition: The side opposite the right.
senses.example: The bakery is on the left after the corner.

senses.definition: Went away or allowed something to stay there. This is a past form of “leave.”
senses.example: Our bus left the station before noon.

senses.definition: An old story that people have passed down, often with parts that may not be true.
senses.example: The guide told us a legend about how the hill got its name.

senses.definition: A key explaining the marks or colors on a map, chart, or picture.
senses.example: The legend shows that green dots mark playgrounds.

senses.definition: Someone remembered for doing something very well or in a memorable way.
senses.example: The coach showed us a photo of a local baseball legend.

senses.definition: The group of people responsible for making laws for a country, state, or other area.
senses.example: The state legislature voted on a proposed law.

senses.definition: A plant in the pea family or a food seed from such a plant.
senses.example: A lentil is a legume you can cook.

senses.definition: A round or oval yellow fruit with sour juice.
senses.example: We squeezed a lemon over the baked potatoes.

senses.definition: To let someone use something for a while, expecting it back.
senses.example: Could you lend me a pencil until the end of class?

senses.definition: How long something is in distance or time.
senses.example: We measured the length of the rug with a tape.

senses.definition: One full stretch of something, such as the distance from one end of a pool to the other.
senses.example: I swam two lengths without stopping.

senses.definition: A piece of clear material that bends light and can help you see things differently.
senses.example: The lens in my magnifying glass made the print look larger.

senses.definition: A large wild cat found in Africa and Asia that usually has dark spots.
senses.example: The leopard rested on a branch above the ground.

senses.definition: A time of teaching or a part of a course that teaches one topic.
senses.example: Our music lesson taught us to count four beats.

senses.definition: An idea or skill you learn from what happens to you.
senses.example: Missing the bus taught me a lesson about checking the time.

senses.definition: To allow something to happen or allow someone to do something.
senses.example: Mom let us stay outside until the porch lights came on.

senses.definition: To suggest doing something, often in “let’s.”
senses.example: Let’s take turns choosing a song.

senses.definition: A disappointment when something is not as good as you expected.
senses.example: It was a letdown when the game ended early because of rain.

senses.definition: A written message to someone.
senses.example: I sent my cousin a letter with a photo inside.

senses.definition: A written sign in an alphabet.
senses.example: Her name starts with the letter D.

senses.definition: A leafy plant often eaten raw in salads or sandwiches.
senses.example: She slid a crisp lettuce leaf into her sandwich.

senses.definition: A height, amount, stage, or rank.
senses.example: The rain raised the water level in the stream.

senses.definition: Flat and even, with no part higher than another.
senses.example: We chose a level space to set up the table.

senses.definition: To make something flat or even.
senses.example: They used a rake to level the ground.

senses.definition: A stiff bar that turns around a point and helps move something.
senses.example: A seesaw is a lever with a support under its middle.

senses.definition: A place or service where people can read, borrow, or use shared books and other materials.
senses.example: We borrowed a book about sharks from the library.

senses.definition: A collection of related materials kept together for people to use.
senses.example: Our teacher kept a library of animal sounds for the project.

senses.definition: A card or digital account number that shows you are allowed to borrow things from a library.
senses.example: I used my library card to check out books about boats.

senses.definition: Official permission to do something, or a document showing that permission.
senses.example: My aunt brought her fishing license when we went out in the boat.

senses.definition: To give official permission for someone to do something or use something.
senses.example: The artist licensed the school to print her drawing in the booklet.

senses.definition: A partnership in which a fungus grows with an alga or a tiny organism that can make sugars from light.
senses.example: The gray lichen grew on the fence post.

senses.definition: To pass your tongue over something.
senses.example: The dog licked the water from its bowl.

senses.definition: One touch or pass of the tongue over something.
senses.example: The calf gave my hand a lick.

senses.definition: A cover that fits over the opening of a container.
senses.example: I found a lid for the soup pot.

senses.definition: To rest or place yourself flat. The past form for this meaning is “lay.”
senses.example: I lay on the rug to play with the puppy.

senses.definition: To say something you know is untrue in order to mislead. The past form for this meaning is “lied.”
senses.example: I would rather tell the truth than lie about a broken toy.

senses.definition: Something said that the speaker knows is not true.
senses.example: I knew it was a lie because I had seen what happened.

senses.definition: The way a person or group usually lives, including what they do day to day.
senses.example: Living near the ocean is part of their outdoor lifestyle.

senses.definition: All the years someone lives or the whole time something lasts.
senses.example: The tree shed its leaves many times during its lifetime.

senses.definition: A force, often from moving air, that acts across the direction of motion and can hold an aircraft up.
senses.example: The glider’s wings made enough lift to stay in the air.

senses.definition: A strong band of body tissue that helps join bones and guide motion at a joint.
senses.example: A ligament helps keep the bones of the knee steady.

senses.definition: A kind of energy that lets our eyes see things when it reaches them.
senses.example: Light from the window fell across the book.

senses.definition: Easy to lift because it weighs little.
senses.example: The empty backpack was light.

senses.definition: Pale in color.
senses.example: I mixed white paint into the dark blue to make it light blue.

senses.definition: To make a place bright or make a lamp start shining.
senses.example: Two lanterns light the path.

senses.definition: The distance light can travel in one year, about 9.5 trillion kilometers.
senses.example: The next star is more than four light-years from the Sun.

senses.definition: A sudden flash of electricity in a storm, often seen as a bright streak in the sky.
senses.example: We saw lightning before we heard the thunder.

senses.definition: Expected to happen or be true.
senses.example: Rain is likely this evening, so we moved the picnic indoors.

senses.definition: Probably.
senses.example: We will likely arrive around noon.

senses.definition: In the same way, or also.
senses.example: Mara likes the shady path, and I likewise prefer it on hot days.

senses.definition: A kind of rock made mostly of calcium carbonate, the material in many shells and corals.
senses.example: Water slowly made a cave in the limestone.

senses.definition: The largest amount or highest point allowed or possible.
senses.example: The pool has a limit of ten people in each class.

senses.definition: To keep the size, amount, or number from going above a point.
senses.example: We limited the number of slices so everyone could have some.

senses.definition: To walk unevenly, often because one foot or leg hurts.
senses.example: She limped to the bench after twisting her ankle.

senses.definition: Not stiff or firm enough to hold its shape.
senses.example: The wet paper was too limp to stand up.

senses.definition: A long, narrow mark.
senses.example: Draw a straight line under the heading.

senses.definition: A row of people or things.
senses.example: We waited in line for the library to open.

senses.definition: A row of words or a stretch of speech in a play.
senses.example: I practiced my first line before the show.

senses.definition: To cover the inside surface of something.
senses.example: We lined the tray with paper before adding cookies.

senses.definition: A cloth made from the fibers of the flax plant.
senses.example: The linen shirt dried quickly after it got wet.

senses.definition: Cloth items such as sheets and tablecloths, usually called “linens.”
senses.example: We folded the clean linens for the guest room.

senses.definition: To stay longer than expected or to go away slowly.
senses.example: The smell of toast lingered after breakfast.

senses.definition: Something that connects two things, such as a ring in a chain or an item on a page that opens another page.
senses.example: I tapped the link to read about the Moon.

senses.definition: To join or connect things.
senses.example: We linked the paper rings to make a chain.

senses.definition: A large wild cat with a loud roar. Many male lions grow a thick mane around the head and neck.
senses.example: A lion rested in the shade while its cubs played.

senses.definition: A kind of matter that flows and takes the shape of the part of a container it fills.
senses.example: The same liquid fit into a tall glass and a wide bowl.

senses.definition: Able to flow like water or another fluid.
senses.example: Sunshine changed the ice into liquid water.

senses.definition: To pay attention to a sound or to what someone is saying.
senses.example: Listen for the bell before you leave your seat.

senses.definition: Trash that has been left in the wrong place.
senses.example: We picked up litter along the edge of the playground.

senses.definition: A group of young animals, such as puppies, born at one time.
senses.example: The dog had a litter of five puppies.

senses.definition: To leave trash lying around or cover a place with scattered things.
senses.example: A storm left branches littering the trail.

senses.definition: Small in size or young in age.
senses.example: A little turtle was hiding under the leaves.

senses.definition: Small in amount or almost none.
senses.example: There was little room left in the box.

senses.definition: To a small degree or hardly at all.
senses.example: The team’s plan changed little after the meeting.

senses.definition: Full of energy and activity.
senses.example: A lively song got everyone moving at the party.

senses.definition: An organ that sorts and changes some things brought by the blood and makes a liquid that helps digest fats.
senses.example: The liver makes bile which can reach the small intestine.

senses.definition: Skills, knowledge, and practices that people learn from earlier generations and keep using.
senses.example: Teaching the next group of dancers kept the village’s living heritage going.

senses.definition: A shore protected from erosion with natural materials such as plants, sand, or oyster reefs.
senses.example: Oysters grew along the living shoreline beside the bay.

senses.definition: A reptile with scales that usually has four legs and a long tail.
senses.example: A little lizard rested on the sun-warmed wall.

senses.definition: Something being carried, lifted, or supported.
senses.example: The crane lifted a load of bricks.

senses.definition: To put something in or on something else so it can be carried or used.
senses.example: We loaded the wagon with books.

senses.definition: A word that people speaking one language take from another language and start using.
senses.example: A word may become a loanword when cooks teach other people the name of a dish.

senses.definition: In or from the place nearby.
senses.example: We bought apples from a local farm.

senses.definition: A person who lives in the place being talked about.
senses.example: A local told us where to find the rocky path to the beach.

senses.definition: To find where someone or something is.
senses.example: We used a map to locate the public garden.

senses.definition: The place where someone or something is found or where something happens.
senses.example: The flyer gives the location of the concert.

senses.definition: A device that keeps something shut or in place until the right key or code is used.
senses.example: The lock on my bike uses a four-number code.

senses.definition: To close something so that it cannot be opened without a key, code, or release.
senses.example: We locked the shed after putting away the rake.

senses.definition: A room or open space just below a roof or above the main floor.
senses.example: We stored the sled in a loft above the garage.

senses.definition: A way of checking how ideas fit together and whether a conclusion follows from the facts or rules.
senses.example: Using logic, we knew the red key had to be in the last box.

senses.definition: An account name and sometimes other information used to sign in to a device or website.
senses.example: I entered my school login to open the reading page.

senses.definition: Feeling sad because you are alone or feel left out.
senses.example: I felt lonely at lunch until someone invited me over.

senses.definition: Measuring a lot from one end to the other.
senses.example: We used a long rope to mark the starting line.

senses.definition: Lasting a lot of time.
senses.example: It was a long wait before the bus came.

senses.definition: To want something very much, often for a long time.
senses.example: I longed to see my cousins again.

senses.definition: A measure in degrees of how far east or west a place is from a line called the prime meridian.
senses.example: Latitude and longitude together help us find a point on a globe.

senses.definition: A long, narrow boat that people used in the Viking Age, with a sail and places for oars.
senses.example: The crew rowed the longship away from the shore.

senses.definition: To turn your eyes toward something or try to find something by watching.
senses.example: Look at the red bird on the fence.

senses.definition: To seem a certain way.
senses.example: Those dark clouds look heavy with rain.

senses.definition: A way that someone or something appears.
senses.example: Her look of surprise made me laugh.

senses.definition: To think or make plans for what will happen later.
senses.example: We can look ahead and pack a raincoat if the forecast changes.

senses.definition: To remember and think about something that happened earlier.
senses.example: When I look back on that race, I remember the cheering.

senses.definition: To feel happy about something that has yet to happen.
senses.example: I look forward to seeing what color the chicks will be.

senses.definition: To pay attention so you notice someone or something when they appear.
senses.example: Look out for the blue backpack on the luggage belt.

senses.definition: To watch over someone and try to keep them safe.
senses.example: My big cousin says he will look out for me in the crowd.

senses.definition: To check something by reading or looking through it fairly quickly.
senses.example: Can you look over the invitation and make sure it has the right date?

senses.definition: To search for a particular piece of information in a source.
senses.example: I can look up the frog’s name in a guide to pond animals.

senses.definition: To respect someone and see them as a person you might learn from.
senses.example: I look up to my uncle because he listens carefully before giving advice.

senses.definition: A tool or frame that holds threads steady for weaving.
senses.example: A weaver stretched white threads across the loom.

senses.definition: In programming, a group of steps that can run repeatedly.
senses.example: A loop tells the game to move the bird a small distance again and again.

senses.definition: Not held, tied, or fitted tightly.
senses.example: A loose wheel made the wagon rattle.

senses.definition: Free or not kept inside a place.
senses.example: Two sheep got loose after the gate swung open.

senses.definition: To stop having something or be unable to find it.
senses.example: I lost one mitten on the way home.

senses.definition: To finish a game, race, or contest without winning.
senses.example: We might lose the match, but we can still play our best.

senses.definition: The state of no longer having something or someone, or the amount that is gone.
senses.example: A loss of paint from the spill left us with only half a can.

senses.definition: A game or contest that you did not win.
senses.example: The team talked about what to practice after the loss.

senses.definition: Making a strong sound that is easy to hear.
senses.example: The rain was loud on the metal roof.

senses.definition: Very pleasant to see, hear, or experience.
senses.example: What a lovely place to sit and read.

senses.definition: Staying true to a person, group, or promise, especially when there is a reason to leave.
senses.example: Her loyal friend still came to visit when she moved to a new school.

senses.definition: Having a good thing happen by chance.
senses.example: We were lucky to see a rainbow just as the clouds cleared.

senses.definition: Suitcases, bags, and other containers you take when you travel.
senses.example: We placed our luggage beside the hotel desk.

senses.definition: A gentle song meant to help a child fall asleep.
senses.example: Grandma sang a lullaby to the baby.

senses.definition: Wood cut into boards or other pieces for building.
senses.example: The workers stacked lumber beside the frame of the shed.

senses.definition: To move in slow, heavy steps.
senses.example: The bear lumbered across the path.
